altloc.rule: one altloc per residue: highest mean occupancy over the residue's atoms, ties broken by first letter; retained atoms written with a blank altloc and their original occupancy

hetero.rule: drop water always; keep any component with a heavy atom within 5.0 A of the retained peptide (flagged additive_in_peptide_site when it is on the crystallisation additive list); keep components covalently or metal-bonded to a retained polymer per _struct_conn; keep curated cofactors within 6.0 A of a retained receptor chain; keep metal ions with >=2 protein donor atoms within 3.0 A; drop everything else and record it

hydrogens.rule: all H/D deleted from every output file

peptide_copy.rule: (0) must contact a protein chain in the deposited asymmetric unit; then (1) most modelled residues, (2) most modelled heavy atoms, (3) highest mean occupancy, (4) lowest mean B, (5) lowest label_asym_id

receptor_chains.rule: keep every protein chain with >=1 heavy-atom pair within 4.5 A of the retained peptide; the largest-BSA chain is always kept, further chains are kept when BSA >= 40 A^2 or contact pairs >= 5; non-contacting protein chains are dropped and recorded

bfactors.note: the ratio is the primary figure: absolute B scales with resolution and refinement protocol, the ratio does not

clashes.convention: van der Waals overlap greater than 0.4 A between non-bonded heavy atoms (MolProbity convention and MolProbity radii). Pairs at bond-graph distance 1, 2 or 3 are excluded - 1-4 exclusion is mandatory without hydrogens because the para pair of every aromatic ring sits at 2.70-2.78 A. The bond graph is CCD bonds + polymer C(i)-N(i+1) + _struct_conn + distance-inferred links, so a macrocycle closure or a staple never registers as a clash. Metals are excluded entirely. Hydrogens are absent, so these counts are NOT on the same scale as the deposited clashscore.

copy_rmsd.note: superposed = Kabsch on the common atoms; in_place = no superposition

deposited_clashes.note: reconstructed by pairing the per-atom <clash> records of the wwPDB report by their cid and discarding any pair with a hydrogen; this is the only apples-to-apples comparison with our heavy-atom-only count, because clashscore itself counts riding hydrogens added by reduce

peptide_rscc.note: RSCC is the direct answer to whether the peptide is in the density and it is available for non-standard components

peptide_rsrz.note: RSRZ is reported only for components with a reference distribution, i.e. essentially only standard residues; for a modified peptide most residues have none, which is why RSCC and not RSRZ is the primary density figure here

geometry.bond_reference: bond lengths from the CCD ideal coordinates of each component; note that the deposited wwPDB report does not check bond geometry for non-standard components at all, so for this corpus there is no other source

occupancy.note: occupancies are those of the retained altloc; an atom below 1.0 here is either a partial-occupancy atom or the retained branch of an alternate conformation

peptide.cif.role: unchanged; every component in it is peptide-integral by construction
